title: Feeling really good about my scene transitions after I spent the past 2 weeks re-building the UI for my Card Scalper game!
author: Ohgood9002
selftext:
I'm still having some issues with the "impact line" effect that fires off when building combos, but i'm honestly feeling really good with the progress I've made

I'm building this fully in GODOT 4.6.  Claude is helping with the the backend and codex to help with some of the frontend stuff. Obviously lots of manual tweaking as well.  

Game doesn't have a wishlist page yet, or anything. i'm still very early on in development but the working title is **Mutura**

comments.author: slipperyslips
comments.body: Cool! I just started drafting a dungeon crawler card game while codex works actuall work. How well is godot codex integretion?

replies.author: Ohgood9002
replies.body:
Pretty good, and it's gotten even better over the past couple of weeks with some updates. Claude does all the heavy lifting for me and is mostly backend and systems design. Codex is really good for building on top of what claude has already done, so i mostly use it for the front end.

The scene transitions and all visual feedback was made with codex. Codex also did the placeholder art for all 120 card designs. I've pivoted to a 1970's Futurism look and need to re-do the card art. The placeholders are fine until i'm ready to tackle that

replies.author: mskuchiki
replies.body: What do you use to control Godot with Claude and Codex? MCP, computer use, Skills?

replies.author: Ohgood9002
replies.body:
I built my own custom agent scaffolding within my GODOT project. All project design documentation was also converted to .MD files for the agents to access. The agents can edit a re-write a variety of .MD files to "talk" to each other and implement the project design cleanly. 

I still run sanity checks and do manual project documentation alignments to catch fringe cases, and a large amount of time is dedicated to cleaning up bugs. Within GODOT everything done within the 2D editor that isnt pure code is pretty much all me. 

Im honestly not using many skills for the agents because they're operating off the .MD files in my scaffolding. I do have a few basic GODOT plug-ins installed for 2D drawing, shaders, etc but the agents are going into my project mostly naked
